extracted.intended_audience: literary critics, periodical reviewers, and editors of literary journals
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and principles for composing and conducting fair, philosophical, and effective literary criticism in periodical reviews, with specific application to poetry and poetical style. Emphasizes announcing principles, grounding judgments in argument and evidence, and stylistic/technical criteria for evaluating poetic language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fair and philosophical inquisition
rubrics_metrics.description: A critic should conduct a fair and philosophical inquiry into a poet’s character as a poet, grounded on the evidence of published works and not on comparative or personal prejudice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Announce and establish the principles you hold as the foundation of poetry in general, specify their application to different classes of poetry, then particularize passages to which they apply, noting frequency, recurrence, and what is characteristic versus accidental. Present premises and deductions so that errors, if any, are tangible and can be detected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Announce critical canons before application
rubrics_metrics.description: Before passing praise or condemnation, the critic should explicitly state the principles (canons) of criticism they use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ground your code on universal morals and philosophic reason, applicable independent of specific works; this allows readers (and poets) to judge your conclusions in the light of your stated premises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Particularize evidence and frequency
rubrics_metrics.description: When applying canons, the critic should cite specific striking passages and indicate how often similar merits or defects recur across the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give instances and show whether the features are widespread or isolated; distinguish what is characteristic of the author's style from accidental lapses or singular beauties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid personal allusion and use only published evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Criticism must address the work, not the author’s private life or outside knowledge; using non-public personal traits to indict the author is improper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Personal attacks convert criticism into gossip or pasquinade; limit remarks to what the publications themselves reveal and do not re-commit or drag forward juvenile or forgotten works for private malice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Faithfulness to announced editorial plan
rubrics_metrics.description: A periodical should adhere to its declared plan: review works deserving argumentative criticism and leave trifling works to sink by their own weight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid criticising works of little importance merely to gratify malignity or to sell copies; example cited: unnecessary treatment of a sermon in an early review number.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground judgments in argument, not assertion
rubrics_metrics.description: Substitute argument for assertion: do not offer broad verdicts without logical support and evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide general grounds or rules from which a claimed fault is deduced; unsupported sweeping statements (e.g., 'This won't do!') are inadequate and unjust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use quotations responsibly to illustrate points
rubrics_metrics.description: When extracting passages to support a verdict, include them with reference to the general grounds and show how they exemplify the claimed quality or defect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid detached extracts that simply illustrate preconceived opinions; extracts should be used to explain the critic's meaning and to demonstrate the justice of the sentence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not cherry-pick to confirm preconceived opinions
rubrics_metrics.description: A critic should not write a critique in advance and then select passages to fit those preconceived judgments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure selection of examples follows careful reading and reasoned judgment rather than being chosen post hoc to illustrate a prewritten verdict.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish character of the critic from that of the work
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep severity or asperity of style directed at the work (its qualities) rather than as personal invective against the author.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sarcasm and censure are permissible in so far as they address the impersonation of the work; avoid personal insults or evidence derived from private knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administer judgment as a representative body when collective
rubrics_metrics.description: If a committee or collective reviews, its members should suspend individuality and pledge to judge according to an agreed constitution or code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This confers authority and dignity upon collective criticism; the code should be grounded on morals and philosophic reason so each speaks as representative of the body corporate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make errors detectable and remediable
rubrics_metrics.description: When the critic errs, present the error in a definite place and tangible form so that readers or the poet can detect and correct it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expose the premises and deductions clearly; an error presented this way 'holds the torch and guides the way to their detection.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Be mindful of rhetorical effect and tone
rubrics_metrics.description: The critic must know the effect they wish to produce and weigh words accordingly; tone is a tool to achieve intended effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose how soft or hard, friendly or bitter your phrases should be in light of the effect you want; imprudent tone can misrepresent critique as vindictiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid substituting personality for criticism
rubrics_metrics.description: Using private malice or republishing forgotten juvenile faults is a mark of personal spite, not of legitimate criticism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such behaviour degrades the critic to a gossip and corrupts the place (the review) meant as sanctuary for reasoned discourse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus reviews on works suitable for argumentative criticism
rubrics_metrics.description: Prioritize books and pamphlets that invite argumentative treatment; do not expend critical energy on ephemeral or trivial productions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Edinburgh Review’s value derived from reviewing works susceptible to argument and from original essays on major subjects; emulate this selectivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize and evaluate poet’s declared theory
rubrics_metrics.description: If an author has publicly stated poetic principles (e.g., Wordsworth’s preface), the critic should evaluate how well those principles are argued and whether they influenced the poems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Point out where an author's theory fails, distinguish truths blended with error, and show how influence appears (diffuse, sporadic, woven in, or separable).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess recognizability and individuality of diction
rubrics_metrics.description: A poet's diction that is peculiarly his own (signature style or recurring tropes) is an evaluative criterion: assess how recognizable, inimitable, and characteristic it is.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: recurring phrases ('The Child is father of the Man'), characteristic images, or modes of expression that make lines independently quotable; note proportion of passages that stand alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate grammatical and syntactic devices as stylistic choices
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify and judge deliberate grammatical peculiarities (e.g., asyndeton, apposition, unusual constructions) as conscious stylistic devices rather than mere errors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether constructions like omission of connectives or appositional phrases serve expressive/poetic ends; do not dismiss them because they differ from ordinary speech.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for elevated diction when conceptually required
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of polysyllabic or 'dictionary' words is defensible where the number and variety of conceptions call for precision; judge such diction in context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask whether the words are employed to express the same thought as in ordinary life; precision and variety of conception may require a more elevated vocabulary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid abrupt inconstancy of style within a poem
rubrics_metrics.description: Critique the sudden and unprepared transitions from striking poetic lines to neutral or prosaic style (inconstancy), which can disturb the reader’s expectation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The poet should either elevate surrounding neutral language to support the high passages or arrange transitions more thoughtfully (e.g., Metastasio’s placement of arias after raised recitative).

rubrics_metrics.name: Manage poetic texture to prevent anticlimax/hyperclimax
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure the lower (neutral) tints of language are raised appropriately so that commanding poetic lines do not create unpleasant alternation of feeling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the lower style is left too low, metre only reminds the reader of an unfulfilled claim; frequent occurrences produce alternating starts of anticlimax and hyperclimax.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judge an author's experiments proportionally
rubrics_metrics.description: When an author experiments with a particular theory or style (e.g., selecting mean forms of human nature), evaluate how widespread and integral the experiment’s influence is relative to the whole body of work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine whether such experiments are isolated and separable or diffusively inwoven into the poet’s works before condemning the poet’s character broadly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the poem’s own occasions and materials in judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider whether a critic has understood and used the opportunities presented by a poem’s implied character, materials, and life-experiences of its speakers when judging appropriateness of character or style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: condemning an itinerant, meditative character by focusing on trivial pack-wares rather than the landscape, solitude, and varied imagery of itinerant life is a flawed approach.
